newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P assigns Rome AA- lira, foreign currency rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns Rome AA- lira, foreign currency rating.

text.p: Credit rating agency Standard & Poor's said it had assigned the city of Rome a long-term counterparty rating of AA minus for both lira and foreign currency debt, with a stable outlook.
S&P said its rating was based on the city's strong economy, its excellent liquidity and its considerable efforts to bring its debt to a reasonable level.

The rating was affected by Rome's weak financial performance in the last few years, mainly due to extraordinary spending to cover debt accumulated in the past by municipal companies and by the considerable borrowing needs for transport infrastructure.

"The considerable restructuring effort undertaken by the city and the consistent reduction of the burden of municipal companies should allow Rome to post positive financial results once the extraordinary expenditure has run its course," S&P said.
"Despite the huge capital account spending plan, Rome's debt should remain under control thanks to the considerable state subsidies and to income deriving from sell-offs," it said.
